title: Alpha Engine attractiveness_eval artifact (eval-storage contract, v2)
description: FROZEN cross-repo contract for backtest/{date}/attractiveness_eval.json — produced by crucible-backtester analysis/attractiveness_eval.py, consumed by crucible-evaluator. Measures the universe-board attractiveness composite against realized forward market-relative log-alpha (config#1389 per-pillar IC + suggested weights, config#1392 trajectory forward-IC, config#1398 top-N counterfactual vs live tech_score gate). All alpha values are DECIMAL log-alpha (0.043 = 4.3%), never percent. Missing/immature sub-blocks carry honest null values and n-fields — never fabricated zeros. Additive-only evolution: consumers MUST tolerate unknown extra fields; renames/removals require a schema_version bump coordinated with the consumer. LIFTED from crucible-backtester contracts/attractiveness_eval.schema.json into nousergon_lib.contracts on the second-adoption signal (config#1861). V2 CHANGE (config#1861, horizon-is-a-parameter doctrine — ARCHITECTURE §48 / config#1483): counterfactual mean_alpha_21d is renamed to mean_alpha in both top_n[] and live_gate — the horizon is given by the top-level horizon_days parameter and must not be hardcoded into the field name. Consumers keep a v1 (mean_alpha_21d) read-tolerance window for 1 week after the coordinated cutover per S3 contract safety.

schema_version.description: Contract version stamp — matches nousergon_lib.contracts.SCHEMA_VERSIONS['attractiveness_eval']. Bumped 1→2 for the mean_alpha_21d→mean_alpha rename (config#1861).

horizon_days.description: Forward-return horizon in trading days, from nousergon_lib.quant.horizons.DEFAULT_POLICY.primary_horizon (21 under the canonical-alpha framework) — a parameter, never hardcoded by the producer. As of v2 the counterfactual alpha field name (mean_alpha) no longer duplicates this horizon.

reason.description: Present when status != ok (or on degraded sub-blocks): the honest, human-readable insufficiency.

pillar_ic.description: Per-pillar date-clustered ICs (config#1389). Keys are the pillar column names of the attractiveness history parquet (schema authority: crucible-research scoring/attractiveness_history.py — currently quality/value/momentum/growth/stewardship/defensiveness; keys are dynamic so a research-side pillar change flows through).

suggested_pillar_weights.description: SUGGESTED weights only — advisory content inside this eval artifact. The producer NEVER writes config/factor_attractiveness_weights.json or any live config. IC-proportional weights shrunk toward 1/N (DeMiguel/Garlappi/Uppal); sum to 1.0 when non-empty.

lambda.description: Weight on the 1/N prior. 1.0 at n_eval_dates <= 8 (the suggested weights ARE 1/N), decaying as 8/n above.

trajectory_ic.description: Forward-IC of the persisted attractiveness-trajectory signals (config#1392), from scanner/universe/trajectory/{date}/trajectory.json joined to realized forward alpha.

counterfactual.description: Top-N-by-attractiveness selections vs the live tech_score survivor gate (config#1398). capture_rate = per-cycle fraction of the cycle's ex-post top-K realized-alpha names (K = selection size, winners from the full scanner-evaluated cycle universe) present in the selection, averaged equally across cycles. mean_alpha = per-cycle selection mean realized forward log-alpha over horizon_days, averaged equally across cycles (date-clustered, decimal). Renamed from mean_alpha_21d in v2 (config#1861): the horizon is carried by the top-level horizon_days, not the field name. ADDITIVE (alpha-engine-config-I7213, no schema_version bump — new optional fields only, per the additive-only evolution rule above): every top_n row and live_gate now also carry a population leg (population_mean_alpha, excess_vs_population, excess_t, excess_p, excess_ci95), and the block carries holding_rule. These are OPTIONAL in the contract, not required: artifacts written before the I7213 producer landed (e.g. backtest/2026-08-07/attractiveness_eval.json) are valid v2 documents without them, and consumers grade an honest N/A naming the missing field rather than failing validation.

n_cycles.description: Independent eval_dates contributing to this row. A cycle with fewer scored names than n is SKIPPED, never truncated, so a row's n_cycles may be below the block-level n_cycles.

population_mean_alpha.description: Equal-weighted mean realized forward log-alpha of the FULL point-in-time cycle universe (every scanner-evaluated name with a realized forward outcome that cycle — NOT the scored subset, or a selector covering only part of the cycle could shrink its own comparator), per cycle then averaged equally across cycles. Scoped to THIS row's cycle set: a cohort skips cycles that cannot fill it, so two rows with different n_cycles legitimately carry different population means. Null when no cycle contributed.

excess_vs_population.description: basket mean alpha MINUS population mean alpha, computed as the mean of the PER-CYCLE paired differences (never the difference of two independently pooled means) — one observation per eval_date. This is the top-N-basket-vs-population read (alpha-engine-config-I7213). Decimal log-alpha over horizon_days, on top of an already market-relative (SPY-subtracted) alpha frame: do not subtract a benchmark again.

excess_t.description: One-sample t-statistic of the per-cycle excess series against zero. Null below the 3-cycle floor, or when the series is degenerate (non-finite) — never fabricated.

excess_p.description: Two-sided p-value of excess_t. Null under the same conditions. Date-clustered by construction: N is the number of independent eval_dates, not the number of (date, ticker) pairs — ~20 names x ~14 weeks is ~14 independent observations, not ~280.

excess_ci95.description: [lo, hi] 95% confidence interval on the per-cycle excess mean (t-interval, df = n_cycles - 1). Collapses to a point [mean, mean] on a zero-variance series rather than being reported as null.

population_mean_alpha.description: Equal-weighted mean realized forward log-alpha of the FULL point-in-time cycle universe (every scanner-evaluated name with a realized forward outcome that cycle — NOT the scored subset, or a selector covering only part of the cycle could shrink its own comparator), per cycle then averaged equally across cycles. Scoped to THIS row's cycle set: a cohort skips cycles that cannot fill it, so two rows with different n_cycles legitimately carry different population means. Null when no cycle contributed.

This is the top-N-basket-vs-population read (alpha-engine-config-I7213). Decimal log-alpha over horizon_days, on top of an already market-relative (SPY-subtracted) alpha frame: do not subtract a benchmark again.

excess_ci95.description: [lo, hi] 95% confidence interval on the per-cycle excess mean (t-interval, df = n_cycles - 1). Collapses to a point [mean, mean] on a zero-variance series rather than being reported as null.

live_gate.description: The live tech_score survivor gate (scanner_evaluations.quant_filter_pass == 1) as a basket. Carries the SAME population leg every top_n row carries (alpha-engine-config-I7213) — the incumbent arm's mean_alpha must not be the only basket on the artifact published without the denominator it was drawn against, or a reader comparing it to a top-N cohort silently attributes the whole gap to selection. Same estimator, same paired per-cycle series, same cycles (the block-level n_cycles).

holding_rule.description: The portfolio construction every basket number in this block assumes, stated IN the artifact so a reader who never sees the producer can read mean_alpha / excess_vs_population unambiguously (alpha-engine-config-I7213 §4). One rule per artifact, not per row: it applies identically to every n / sector_balanced variant and to live_gate. Top-N membership turns over several names a day, so a basket return without a stated rebalance and hold rule is not interpretable.

ic_block.description: Date-clustered Spearman rank-IC (each weekly cross-section is ONE observation, Grinold-Kahn t-stat; honest small-N — t/p null below 3 weekly observations) + pooled IC/p as the secondary, pseudo-replication-inflated reference.
